whereTheInterimDisclosureLands.decision: A new NULLABLE BOOLEAN column on the stamped row: `txgio_parcel.zoning_district_interim` (migration `lib/db/drizzle/0103_txgio_parcel_zoning_district_interim.sql`). The mission's item 1 says the disclosure must be carried 'so the stamped row records that the district is interim' and offers 'column, JSON field or provenance note'. `txgio_parcel` has no JSON provenance column, so a column is the only form that actually lands the fact ON THE ROW; the other two would land it only on the run, which is a different claim.
whereTheInterimDisclosureLands.semantics: NULL = nothing was stamped for this parcel (the pre-existing honest-absence state). true = a district was stamped and the published value carried a declared interim qualifier. false = a district was stamped from a published value with no interim qualifier. Explicit false, not NULL, for a stamped non-interim district, so 'stamped and not interim' cannot be read as 'not stamped'.
whereTheInterimDisclosureLands.secondDisclosureSurface: The same fact is carried in the run's provenance as well, because the row alone cannot be read without the run: `ZoningStampSummary.parcelsInterim` + `interimBaseHistogram` (the base each interim value resolved to), the CLI's 'of which interim' line, and `LayerParseAudit.interimBase` / `interimPlannedDevelopment` (the layer-level audit printed before any PIP).
whereTheInterimDisclosureLands.whyNotAParserOnlyFact: The parse result carries `interim: boolean` and travels to the polygon, the PIP index and the stamp summary regardless. That is necessary but not sufficient: the mission's words are 'the stamped row records that the district is interim'.
whereTheInterimDisclosureLands.servePath: NONE reads it today, and this lane builds none (the mission forbids a serve change). Stated plainly: `zoning_district_interim` is written and never read. Nothing in the envelope route, the router, the MCP payload or the PDF consults it. It exists so the fact is recoverable from the store instead of only from a log.
whereTheInterimDisclosureLands.prerequisiteForTheSeat: The integration seat must apply migration 0103 before running the stamp with --apply. The stamp FAILS CLOSED (Postgres errors on an unknown column in the UPDATE, so the very first batch aborts and zero rows are written) rather than silently stamping districts without the disclosure. This is the same prerequisite shape the CLI already documents for migration 0059 (`zoning_district`). Declared here, in the CLI docstring, and in the close.

theInterimRule.config: `BaseCodeParseConfig.interimQualifiers?: readonly string[]`, set to `['I']` on the three Austin registry entries (austin-tx, austin-tx-williamson, austin-tx-hays) as `AUSTIN_INTERIM_QUALIFIERS`.
theInterimRule.rule: When the published value has no direct resolution AND a declared qualifier heads it at a separator boundary, the qualifier is STRIPPED and the SAME rule runs on the remainder: the longest known base district at a separator boundary, then the planned-development pattern, then unrecognised. `I-SF-2-NP` -> base SF-2 with overlay NP and interim true; `I-RR-NP` -> RR with NP; `I-PUD` -> the planned-development route with interim true; `I-SF-4A` -> SF-4A. A qualifier followed by nothing (`I`, `I-`), or by a remainder matching no base (`I-XYZ`), stays `unrecognised` with the reason naming the qualifier.
theInterimRule.vocabularyStaysFirst: The direct resolution is attempted on the whole value BEFORE any qualifier is stripped, so a city that really rows a district whose code starts with a declared qualifier wins over the strip. No divergence from the existing order for any value that already resolved.
theInterimRule.noBehaviourChangeWhenUnconfigured: With `interimQualifiers` absent or empty, `parseBaseCode` returns exactly what it returned before this lane, field for field (the new `interim` field is `false`). The existing falsifier fixtures -- CS-1 longest match, SF-4 unrecognised, SF-4.5 unrecognised, R&D, W/LO, the `-`/`/`/whitespace separator rules, the empty value -- are re-asserted unchanged.
theInterimRule.orderOfTheMeasuredBands: The 14 live interim values move OUT of `unrecognised` (they are 14 of the 31 unrecognised values / 1,229 of the 1,544 unrecognised polygons measured by the predecessor at layer grain). That is the whole point of the lane, and it is why two existing test expectations in `zoningBaseCode.test.ts` (LIVE_SAMPLE['I-SF-2'], LIVE_SAMPLE['I-RR'], LIVE_SAMPLE['I-SF-4A'], the unrecognised-family histogram and the layer-audit bucket test) MUST change: they assert the old behaviour. Named here so the change is a declared consequence of the ruling, not a test edited to go green.

theNoAccountSkip.rule: At stamp time a feature whose `prop_id` is `'0'`, empty/whitespace, or NULL writes no row and is counted by reason. The check runs BEFORE the PIP, so a no-account feature is never stamped by any bucket.
theNoAccountSkip.whereCounted: `ZoningStampSummary.parcelsSkippedNoAccount` + `skippedNoAccountByReason` ('zero' | 'empty' | 'null'). The five-way bucket invariant replaces the four-way one: matched + plannedDevelopment + unrecognised + unmatched + skippedNoAccount == parcelsRead. Nothing is derived by subtraction (DEV-PROCESS 1.3), and no parcel can be silently dropped.
theNoAccountSkip.denominations: `parcelsRead` keeps its existing meaning (distinct `feature_index` read for the county -- the number the predecessor's bands were written in). Three NEW numbers are reported beside it on every leg: `accountsRead` (distinct REAL `prop_id` among the features read), `accountBearingFeatures` (features read minus skipped), and `parcelsSkippedNoAccount`. The CLI prints all three, so no figure travels without its denominator or its denomination (DEV-PROCESS 1.1/1.2).
theNoAccountSkip.interimCounts: `parcelsInterim` counts parcels whose stamped district came through an interim qualifier and whose kind is 'base' (a resolved interim district); `parcelsInterimPlannedDevelopment` counts `I-PUD`-class values. `interimBaseHistogram` names the base each interim value resolved to (the disclosure of WHAT it was read as, not just that it was interim).

adversarialNotes: THE BAND THE PREDECESSOR LEFT BROKEN. Falsifier 1 of the PREDECESSOR lane (P-259) pre-registered a Travis `parcelsRead` band of 380,917 +/- 2% and measured 828,773 -- a 2.18x miss -- because the band was written in ACCOUNT terms and the CLI reports FEATURES. This lane's falsifier 1 band is therefore written in the denomination the instrument actually prints, and the denomination is stated beside every number in the table. The predecessor's PARTIAL is inherited, not re-graded.

THE INTERIM VALUES ARE NOT ALL NUMBERED. `I-AV` (1 polygon) is in the live family and is easy to miss (it does not appear in any of the three county dry-run histograms the predecessor printed, because its one polygon covers no sampled parcel). The 14-value test is driven off the FIXTURE'S vocabulary (`allDistinctValues`), not off the parcel histograms, so a value that stamps nothing is still covered.

THE DISCLOSURE IS A ROW FACT, NOT A LOG FACT. Writing it only to the CLI's output would make it unrecoverable from the store and would not satisfy 'the stamped row records that the district is interim'. The column is the decision; the log is the second copy.

A GREEN TEST SUITE IS NOT THE GRADE. Two of the four falsifiers are statements about a staging run; the unit tests can be fully green with the dry-run table wrong, which is why the table is produced and transcribed literally rather than summarised.
